_comment: Third real (non-dry) retraining run -- WBS 4.3.5, 2026-08-27, Colab T4.
This run was explicitly meant to be the LAST retrain before locking a
candidate for the thesis. A pre-flight audit on 2026-08-26/27 found two
silent data-corruption bugs that the 2026-08-26 run's candidate trained
under, both fixed before this run:
1. 163 human-confirmed review corrections (DISAGREE verdicts with a
correct_label, from 8 historical review sheets) were never re-applied
after the 2026-08-26 rebuild -- apply_review_corrections.py exists to
do exactly this but wasn't run/didn't stick. Root-cause fixed by
wiring the correction step directly into build_dataset.py's main(),
so every future rebuild auto-applies it.
2. Discovered while re-running the fix: apply_review_corrections.py
itself read from a HARDCODED list of 8 sheet filenames, so the two
new sheets reviewed today (review_sheet_2026-08-26.csv, 694 rows;
review_sheet_backlog_gap_2026-08-26.csv, 67 rows) were silently
skipped on the first rebuild attempt -- the same class of bug as (1).
Fixed by switching to auto-discovery of any review_sheet*.csv in
datasets/audit/.
With both fixed, this run's rebuild applied 328 corrections total (163
historical + 165 new from today's two sheets), vs. the 163 the 2026-08-26
candidate actually trained under. Same 21,571-row raw pool / 18,938
unique-after-holdout-exclusion structure as 2026-08-26 -- WBS 6.4.6's
holdout set (datasets/holdout/holdout.csv, frozen 2026-08-18) was
reconfirmed at 0 overlap before this run.
Dependency pins were also locked exactly (transformers==4.57.6,
datasets==4.0.0, accelerate==1.14.0, huggingface-hub==0.36.2) after the
2026-08-26 run's mid-run transformers-v5 crash -- reused known-good exact
versions instead of letting Colab's pip re-resolve, so this run installed
clean with no crash.
Committed here rather than beside the checkpoint because ai/models/*/ is
git-ignored. The candidate weights (~1.1 GB) live only in Google Drive at
MyDrive/bantai/retraining_runs/, per the notebook's own step 10 guidance
(regenerable from this manifest: same labeled dataset, same seed 42, same
training code -- no reason to pull the weights unless promoting or
running the holdout evaluation).
READ THE VERDICT AS A RECOMMENDATION, NOT AN INSTRUCTION. Nothing was
promoted. See _interpretation below.

baseline_checkpoint._comment: The currently-deployed ai/models/xlm-roberta-smishing/ -- unchanged since the 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-26 runs; still nothing has been promoted.

decision.reason: significantly better: 193 fixes vs 76 regressions (p=0.0000), macro-F1 0.9225 -> 0.9461

zero_reports_was_deliberate: Same as the 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-26 runs: no validated user reports
exist yet (mobile's report flow is navigation-only, not wired to the
backend), so the manifest records 'null (no report store consulted)'
rather than a zero that could be misread as 'none were filed'.
why_this_scores_slightly_higher_than_the: Baseline macro-F1 moved from 0.9186 (08-26 run) to 0.9225, and candidate
macro-F1 moved from 0.9451 to 0.9461. Both are measured against the
same held-out validation split mechanism (seed=42) but drawn from a
dataset with 165 additional label corrections applied that the 08-26
run's data was missing -- see _comment. The direction of those
corrections (net Ham -> Spam/Scam, from today's two review sheets) is a
plausible, modest driver of the small score shift in both directions;
not a large effect, which is expected since only ~1% of the pool
what_drove_the_improvement_over_the_depl: Same story as 2026-08-26: fix transitions skew heavily Spam->Ham (108)
and Ham->Spam (56), meaning most of the improvement over the currently-
deployed model is the candidate learning to tell honest marketing/promo
apart from personal/transactional messages more reliably -- consistent
with the raw-inbox batches folded in since the baseline's 2026-07-29
training date being real, everyday phone traffic rather than curated
why_nothing_was_promoted_yet: Same reasoning as both prior runs, and it still applies: promoting
checkpoint's embedding space) and invalidates the Sprint 5 calibration
numbers signed off by the adviser on 2026-08-26. This candidate is the
one meant to go to the adviser as the actual promotion decision -- it is
the first trained on genuinely finalized data (all known review
corrections applied, holdout-clean, locked dependency versions) -- but
the decision to swap the deployed model stays a separate, deliberate
step after that conversation, not something this run does on its own.
clean_holdout_evaluation: DONE, same day. scripts/evaluate_holdout.py run against this candidate
-- the first genuinely clean WBS 6.4.6 result (trained after the
2026-08-18 holdout freeze, zero leakage, reconfirmed before this run).
Result: macro-F1 0.9592 on 3,236 never-seen rows -- see
than this candidate's own internal validation macro-F1 (0.9461 above),
which is a good sign against overfitting, not a discrepancy to worry
The number that matters most for the thesis: Scam recall is 92.4%
(38 of 498 real scams misclassified as Ham/Spam, a 7.6% miss rate) --
call this out directly as the honest weak point, don't let the strong
macro-F1 bury it. Ham false-positive rate is very low (4 of 1,785,
0.95) is the DEPLOYED baseline measured on a holdout it may have partly
trained on -- still not a clean number, kept for reference only, not a
fair comparison point against this candidate's 0.9592.
known_gap: Same as the prior two runs: the gate records how many messages moved
each way (fix_transitions / regression_transitions), not which specific
ones. The actual disagreeing message bodies exist in this run's
disagreements.json on Drive (git-ignored, contains real SMS text --
never committed) if a specific example is needed for a defense.
